gastronomy:Ichthyoskala Keratsiniou.name: Ichthyoskala Keratsiniou
gastronomy:Ichthyoskala Keratsiniou.teaser: The night's Aegean catch, sung off by the crate under floodlights before most of Piraeus wakes
gastronomy:Ichthyoskala Keratsiniou.story: Since 1965 the fish of half the Aegean has come ashore at Limani Irakleiou, on the Keratsini edge of the port, and the old guide calls it the largest auction in Greece. Trawlers and small gri-gri purse-seiners moor under floodlights after midnight; auctioneers call prices over stacked crates of red mullet, gavros, cuttlefish and squid, and the buyers for the port's tavernas and the Athens fishmongers settle it all before sunrise. Arrive at mid-morning and all that is left is a hosed concrete floor and gulls. This is a working quay, not a food hall.
gastronomy:Ichthyoskala Keratsiniou.why: Go once in the dark: it is where every fish on a Piraeus grill starts the day.
facts: Nightly through the working week; check holiday closures locally
From about midnight; winding down around 06:30 (seen Jul 2026)
The hour before dawn, when the bidding is loudest
Red mullet, gavros, cuttlefish and squid, sold by the crate at wholesale prices; know your species and bargain per crate

gastronomy:Central Market of Piraeus.name: Central Market of Piraeus
gastronomy:Central Market of Piraeus.teaser: The covered shed is half empty; the two blocks around it are the real market
gastronomy:Central Market of Piraeus.story: Treat 'the market' as a district, not a building. The covered hall in Agia Triada stands half empty under the bioclimatic canopy fitted in 2025. Walk the streets around it instead. After 1922 refugees from Smyrna and Anatolia filled this quarter with their shopfronts and three rows of fish stalls, and on Gounari and Tsamadou their trades still run within about 200 metres of each other: cured beef, pastry sheets, roasted nuts, spices from open sacks. Each of those counters has its own card below. Come on foot, on a weekday morning.
gastronomy:Central Market of Piraeus.why: Shop the lanes, not the shed: the old refugee trades are a block away.
facts: Monday to Saturday; most stalls shut on Sunday
The fish rows, then the Asia Minor counters along Gounari and Tsamadou
gastronomy:Central Market of Piraeus.maps_query: Central Market Dimosthenous Lykourgou Agia Triada Piraeus

gastronomy:Avakian.name: Avakian
gastronomy:Avakian.teaser: Cappadocian pastourma cured by one Armenian family since 1922, in an arcade off Gounari
gastronomy:Avakian.story: Aram Avakian came from Kaisareia in Cappadocia to Palia Kokkinia in 1922 and cured his first pastourma on his own rooftop before taking a market stall; his son Giorgos carried the craft on, and Athens Voice notes the shop now trades as 'O Giorgos' while everyone still says Avakian. The family moved into the Stoa Politou arcade when the old market came down in 1967. The beef is air-cured under a red crust of fenugreek and garlic, sold beside spicy soutzouki and kavourma. Ask for it sliced paper-thin: a few slices will flavour a whole plate.
gastronomy:Avakian.why: Have the pastourma cut thin to order, then wrapped for the galley.
facts: Stoa Politou, Dimitriou Gounari 21, Agia Triada; the sign may read 'O Giorgos'

sources.label: Athens Voice: six Piraeus haunts with a long history (Avakian / 'O Giorgos')

gastronomy:Vourloglou.name: Vourloglou
gastronomy:Vourloglou.teaser: A basement pastry counter on Tsamadou, by the old guide's account; confirm it before you plan around it
gastronomy:Vourloglou.story: Our earlier guide described a basement workshop at Tsamadou 1, behind an unmarked door, where the brothers Kostas and Dimitris Vourloglou have made phyllo, shredded kataifi and bougatsa since the late 1960s, a pastry craft that traces back to Vourla near Smyrna. The same guide's source list, though, linked vourloglou.gr as a marine chandlery, and a fresh search in October 2026 found no independent mention of a phyllo maker by this name. The name may simply be shared. Until someone sees the bench in person, treat it as unconfirmed and go by the street address.
gastronomy:Vourloglou.why: Worth a look on a market morning, but bring the sheets home only if you find the door.
facts: Tsamadou 1, Agia Triada, below street level (old guide; not re-confirmed Oct 2026)
Phyllo, kataifi, bougatsa (as the old guide reported)

provisioning:Mastronikolas.name: Mastronikolas
provisioning:Mastronikolas.teaser: The port's galaktoboureko, carried down to the boat in a round pan
provisioning:Mastronikolas.story: The galaktopoleio on Karaoli & Dimitriou has stood on the same spot since 1909, and it bakes its galaktoboureko in round pans and big trays, which makes it the one sweet in Piraeus you can bring aboard whole. Its own card is in the tables.
facts: Galaktoboureko by the pan; rizogalo and krema to go with it
Walk in; for a whole tray, phone the counter first (+30 210 4123783). Whether trays are made to order was not confirmed
A few euros a slice (seen Jul 2026); ask for the tray price

gastronomy:Mandragoras.name: Mandragoras
gastronomy:Mandragoras.teaser: Open sacks of mountain oregano and Greek saffron, weighed out on Gounari since 1963
gastronomy:Mandragoras.story: Fotis Vasilopoulos began working at eight, in a grocery in Nafplio, and opened Mandragoras in 1955; it has occupied its spot on Gounari since 1963. The walls are lined with open sacks: wild mountain oregano still on the stem, red Greek saffron weighed from the bag, sun-dried tomatoes, pulses, hand-cut regional pasta, olives from the barrel. Galley chefs and neighbourhood grandmothers stand in the same queue for the oregano. Everything is weighed and wrapped by hand, so the counter moves slowly. Arrive with a written list.
gastronomy:Mandragoras.why: The first stop for a chef restocking dried herbs, pulses and saffron in one place.
facts: Mon, Wed, Sat 08:00–16:00; Tue, Thu, Fri 08:00–20:00; closed Sunday (seen Jul 2026)
Mountain oregano, Greek saffron, pulses, regional pasta, barrel olives

gastronomy:Assos Xiroi Karpoi.name: Assos Xiroi Karpoi
gastronomy:Assos Xiroi Karpoi.teaser: Almonds and pistachios that come off the drum still warm, roasted on Tsamadou since 1948
gastronomy:Assos Xiroi Karpoi.story: The Ovakimians, an Armenian family who brought the roaster's trade with them from Asia Minor, have roasted nuts inside this Tsamadou shop since 1948. The third generation, Agop and his brother Dikran, now run the drum: almonds, pistachios, roasted chickpeas, candied ginger, and dried fruit from all over Greece. You smell it before you see it, hot almonds drifting down the street, the oldest signal the market gives. Buy a bag still warm from the roaster and compare it with any packet nut aboard.
gastronomy:Assos Xiroi Karpoi.why: Ask for whatever has just come out of the roaster.
facts: Market daytime hours; closed Sunday (seen Jul 2026)
Freshly roasted almonds and pistachios, leblebi chickpeas, candied ginger, dried fruit

gastronomy:Dakoutros Marine.name: Dakoutros Marine
gastronomy:Dakoutros Marine.teaser: Four floors of rope, anchors and paint in the chandlers' streets behind the quays
gastronomy:Dakoutros Marine.story: North of the quays, a few streets are given over almost entirely to selling things to ships. Dakoutros has worked there since 1981, across four storeys: rope by the reel, anchors, fenders, safety gear, stainless fittings, navigation lights, marine paint in bulk. It sells no food. It is, though, the other half of a crew's day ashore: the captain buys the anchor shackle a block from where the cook buys the oregano. Walk the surrounding streets too; that trade is as much the port's terroir as the fish auction.
gastronomy:Dakoutros Marine.why: Combine it with the market run: deck stores and galley stores in one walk.
facts: Antiploiarchou Vlachakou 13 at Gravias, north of the central quays
Weekday business hours and Saturday morning (seen Jul 2026)
Rope, anchors, fenders, safety gear, stainless fittings, navigation lights, marine paint

around:Aegina.name: Aegina
around:Aegina.teaser: Forty minutes on a fast boat to the pistachio island and a Doric temple on a pine hill
around:Aegina.story: Aegina is the nearest real island, with boats from Piraeus through the day. In late August its orchards start their pistachio harvest; the nut has been protected as Fistiki Aiginis since the 1990s and growers have pooled their crop in a cooperative since 1947. The temple of Aphaia, on the far side of the island, went up around 500 to 490 BC, Doric, on a pine hill about 160 metres up, some 15 km from the harbour town. Take the bus or a taxi out, then come back to the port for an ouzo with a bag of the year's nuts.
around:Aegina.why: Aphaia in the late afternoon, then pistachios bought in the harbour town.
facts: Fast boats take about 40 minutes and conventional ferries about 1 hour to 1 hour 25 minutes; Saronic ferries usually leave from gate E8, but confirm the gate on your ticket (ferry guides, Oct 2026)
The Temple of Aphaia: Apr–Oct 08:00–20:00, EUR 10 full and EUR 5 reduced (Oct 2026); check winter hours from 1 Nov
Aegina pistachios, roasted or raw, from the harbour town; harvest begins in late August

around:Salamina.name: Salamina
around:Salamina.teaser: A EUR 1.20 ferry across the water where the Greek fleet beat Xerxes in 480 BC
around:Salamina.story: The small car ferries shuttling between Perama and Paloukia cross the narrows where the Greek triremes broke the Persian fleet in September 480 BC. The crossing is so short and so routine that the commuters around you barely look up. On the island, the Kynosoura peninsula south of the port holds the burial mound of the Salamis dead and a view straight back over the strait. Further south, near Peristeria, is the cave where Euripides is said to have written; excavators found a fifth-century BC cup there with his name on it.
around:Salamina.why: Stand on deck for the crossing: the battle strait is the view from the rail.
facts: Ferry from Perama to Paloukia, about 15 minutes, every 15 minutes on weekdays from early morning; about EUR 1.20 a passenger (Ferryhopper, Oct 2026, undated fare)
Half a day; a car or taxi on the island helps
The Salamis fighters' tumulus on Kynosoura, looking over the strait

sources.label: Ferryhopper: how to get to Salamis

around:Hydra.name: Hydra
around:Hydra.teaser: No cars, no scooters, not even bicycles: just stone, mules and water taxis
around:Hydra.story: Local law keeps every motor vehicle off Hydra apart from the refuse and fire trucks and the ambulance, and a rule from the 1950s keeps bicycles off too. So the cargo from the boat goes up the stepped lanes on donkeys and mules, and the coast is served by water taxis. From the harbour, walk west from it past the small pebble beach at Avlaki to Kamini, a fishing harbour with tavernas and swimming rocks; past Kamini the way becomes a partly cobbled coastal path toward Vlychos. Take a water taxi back once your legs give out.
around:Hydra.why: Walk out to Kamini for lunch and a swim off the rocks, not along the harbour front.
facts: High-speed catamarans from Piraeus (Hellenic Seaways, Alpha Lines) take about 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes depending on stops; book ahead in summer and at weekends (Oct 2026)
A long day, first boat out and last boat back
The coastal walk west past Avlaki to Kamini and on toward Vlychos; water taxis come back from both
Kamini's tavernas by the fishing harbour

follow:Port of Piraeus (OLP).name: Port of Piraeus (OLP)
follow:Port of Piraeus (OLP).teaser: Which gate your boat leaves from, and which quay is closed for works
follow:Port of Piraeus (OLP).story: The Piraeus Port Authority runs the busiest passenger port in Europe, and its site is where gate assignments for ferries and cruise ships, the day's departures and notices of berth works are published. The quays stretch a long way around the harbour, and boats to the same island do not always leave from the same gate. Look up your gate here the evening before you sail.
follow:Port of Piraeus (OLP).why: Check your gate before the taxi, not at the quay.
facts: The official site of the Piraeus Port Authority: gate assignments, departures, port works and closures
The ferry and cruise departures pages, and notices of berth works

follow:Hellenic Coast Guard.name: Hellenic Coast Guard
follow:Hellenic Coast Guard.teaser: When the wind stops the ferries, the Coast Guard is the one that says so
follow:Hellenic Coast Guard.story: On days of very strong wind, the Coast Guard bans sailings port by port. The order often targets the high-speed boats first, and in the Saronic it can leave sailings to each captain's call. Bans usually come up for review at fixed hours, so a boat cancelled at dawn may still go by noon. On a meltemi day in July or August, check before leaving for the quay.
follow:Hellenic Coast Guard.why: On a windy summer morning, read this before you buy the ticket.
facts: The Hellenic Coast Guard's official site: sailing bans (apagorefsi apoplou) and safety notices
The day's sailing-ban announcements for the ports of Attica

sources.label: AMNA: sailing ban imposed at ports due to strong winds

follow:Municipality of Piraeus.name: Municipality of Piraeus
follow:Municipality of Piraeus.teaser: Days of the Sea, the Veakeio summer bill and Apokries, straight from the town hall
follow:Municipality of Piraeus.story: The town hall publishes the port's own year: the Days of the Sea festival in late May and June, the summer programme at the open-air Veakeio theatre, and the carnival dates of Apokries, from Tsiknopempti to Clean Monday. Its separate culture portal is the place to look for town events such as the Piraeus Port Film Festival in September and the 6 January Epiphany dive in the harbour. For Athens itself, use the sister guide at /terroir/Athens-Attiki/ instead.
follow:Municipality of Piraeus.why: Check the Veakeio bill before you book a June or July evening.
facts: The official site of the Municipality of Piraeus, with a separate culture portal for events
Days of the Sea, the Veakeio programme, Apokries; the sister guide at /terroir/Athens-Attiki/ covers Athens

follow:Posidonia.name: Posidonia
follow:Posidonia.teaser: The biennial shipping fair that fills every taverna and yacht berth from Mikrolimano to Zea
follow:Posidonia.story: Every even-numbered year in early June, the world's shipowners come to Attica for Posidonia, run by Posidonia Exhibitions SA with the Union of Greek Shipowners and the Hellenic Chamber of Shipping among its backers. The halls are at Metropolitan Expo by the airport, but the dinners are in Piraeus, and for that week the waterfront tables and the marina berths go first. The 2026 edition ran 1 to 5 June. Trade listings put the 30th, in 2028, at 5 to 9 June.
follow:Posidonia.why: If your dates touch the first week of June in an even year, book the tables early.
facts: The organiser's site for the biennial Posidonia shipping exhibition (even years, early June)
Next edition: 5–9 June 2028 at Metropolitan Expo, per trade listings citing the organiser (Oct 2026); confirm on the official site
